  check("estimateOnlyPosture: unrecognised value (typo) fails safe to refuse, NOT warn",
    estimateOnlyPosture({ budget: { on_estimate_only: "wrn" } }) === "refuse");

  // costArmed / tokenDependentCeilingArmed — the token-dependent-ceiling test the
  // budget-metering gate keys off. tokens always counts; cost only when armed
  // (FAFF-427 pricing); until/max_attempts alone never count.
  check("costArmed: pricing:map + cost set is armed", costArmed({ ceilings: { cost: 5 }, pricing: "map" }) === true);
  check("costArmed: pricing:flat + price>0 is armed", costArmed({ ceilings: { cost: 5 }, pricing: "flat", price_per_mtok: 3 }) === true);
  check("costArmed: pricing:flat + price 0 is NOT armed", costArmed({ ceilings: { cost: 5 }, pricing: "flat", price_per_mtok: 0 }) === false);
  check("costArmed: no cost ceiling at all is NOT armed", costArmed({ ceilings: { cost: null }, pricing: "map" }) === false);
  check("tokenDependentCeilingArmed: tokens set is armed", tokenDependentCeilingArmed({ ceilings: { tokens: 100, cost: null }, pricing: "map" }) === true);
  check("tokenDependentCeilingArmed: armed cost is armed", tokenDependentCeilingArmed({ ceilings: { tokens: null, cost: 5 }, pricing: "map" }) === true);
  check("tokenDependentCeilingArmed: until-only is NOT armed (a clock needs no token meter)",
    tokenDependentCeilingArmed({ ceilings: { tokens: null, cost: null, until: "07:00" }, pricing: "map" }) === false);
  check("tokenDependentCeilingArmed: max_attempts-only is NOT armed",
    tokenDependentCeilingArmed({ ceilings: { tokens: null, cost: null, max_attempts: 40 }, pricing: "map" }) === false);

  // lightsOutPreflight: default posture (refuse) with an armed token-dependent ceiling
  // and an estimate-only meter → refuses with gate budget-metering, no degrades.
  const meteringRefuse = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ tokenDependentCeiling: true, meteringMeasurable: false }));
  check("budget-metering: estimate-only + token-dependent ceiling + default posture refuses",
    meteringRefuse.proceed === false && meteringRefuse.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering"));
  check("budget-metering refusal names the fix + the warn opt-out",
    meteringRefuse.refusals.find((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering").detail.includes("budget.on_estimate_only: warn"));
  check("budget-metering refuse path carries no degrades", meteringRefuse.degrades.length === 0);

  // Explicit warn posture: same estimate-only + token-dependent ceiling now PROCEEDS,
  // with a degrades[] entry naming budget-metering (the loud degrade, never silent).
  const meteringWarn = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    tokenDependentCeiling: true, meteringMeasurable: false, estimateOnlyPosture: "warn",
  }));
  check("budget-metering: warn posture proceeds despite estimate-only metering",
    meteringWarn.proceed === true && !meteringWarn.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering"));
  check("budget-metering: warn posture populates degrades[] naming the gate",
    meteringWarn.degrades.some((d) => d.gate === "budget-metering"));
  check("budget-metering: warn-posture banner carries a DEGRADED line",
    /degraded \(proceeding\)/.test(meteringWarn.banner) && meteringWarn.banner.includes("budget-metering"));

  // A MEASURABLE meter never fires the gate, regardless of posture or ceiling shape —
  // the happy path (armedProbes' default) already proves this implicitly, restated here
  // explicitly against a token-dependent ceiling.
  const meteringOk = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ tokenDependentCeiling: true, meteringMeasurable: true }));
  check("budget-metering: measurable meter + token-dependent ceiling proceeds clean",
    meteringOk.proceed === true && meteringOk.degrades.length === 0
    && !meteringOk.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering"));

  // An until-only (or absent) token-dependent-ceiling flag never fires the gate, even
  // with an estimate-only meter and the default refuse posture — a clock needs no meter.
  const meteringUntilOnly = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ tokenDependentCeiling: false, meteringMeasurable: false }));
  check("budget-metering: no token-dependent ceiling never fires the gate (until/count-only governor)",
    meteringUntilOnly.proceed === true && meteringUntilOnly.degrades.length === 0
    && !meteringUntilOnly.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering"));

  // Additive-probe tolerance: an older caller of this pure function that never set
  // `meteringMeasurable` at all is tolerated as measurable — never a surprise refusal.
  const meteringAbsentProbe = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ tokenDependentCeiling: true }));
  check("budget-metering: absent meteringMeasurable probe tolerated as measurable (additive-probe rule)",
    meteringAbsentProbe.proceed === true && !meteringAbsentProbe.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "budget-metering"));

  // FAFF-312 — mint-time at_ceiling default: escalate-when-unset, explicit honoured.
  check("mint at_ceiling: unset → escalate (L4 default)", mintAtCeiling({}) === "escalate");
  check("mint at_ceiling: no budget block → escalate", mintAtCeiling({ budget: {} }) === "escalate");
  check("mint at_ceiling: explicit stop honoured verbatim", mintAtCeiling({ budget: { at_ceiling: "stop" } }) === "stop");
  check("mint at_ceiling: explicit escalate honoured", mintAtCeiling({ budget: { at_ceiling: "escalate" } }) === "escalate");
  check("mint at_ceiling: explicit narrow honoured", mintAtCeiling({ budget: { at_ceiling: "narrow" } }) === "narrow");
  check("mint at_ceiling: unrecognised value (typo) fails safe to escalate, NOT stop", mintAtCeiling({ budget: { at_ceiling: "escalte" } }) === "escalate");

  // --prd-creative-licence flag → ledger prd_creative_licence resolution.
  check("prd licence: absent flag → null (no PRD gate ran)", prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag(null).ok === true && prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag(null).value === null);
  check("prd licence: broad → broad", prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("broad").ok === true && prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("broad").value === "broad");
  check("prd licence: tight → tight", prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("tight").ok === true && prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("tight").value === "tight");
  check("prd licence: off-vocabulary → not ok (fail loud, never a silent null)", prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("wide").ok === false && prdCreativeLicenceFromFlag("wide").value === null);

  // FAFF-515 — --prd-root-container flag → ledger prd_root_container resolution (rides the licence flag).
  check("prd root: absent flag → null record (no PRD gate ran)", prdRootContainerFromFlags(null, null).ok === true && prdRootContainerFromFlags(null, null).value === null);
  check("prd root: container + licence → value persisted", prdRootContainerFromFlags("Top of the loop", "broad").ok === true && prdRootContainerFromFlags("Top of the loop", "broad").value === "Top of the loop");
  check("prd root: container WITHOUT licence → not ok (mint refusal, never a silent null)", prdRootContainerFromFlags("Top of the loop", null).ok === false && prdRootContainerFromFlags("Top of the loop", null).value === null);
  check("prd root: blank container → not ok (a referent naming nothing anchors nothing)", prdRootContainerFromFlags("  ", "tight").ok === false);

  // Keystone (sentry) probe fails → refuse, no reduced mode.
  const noSentry = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ reachable: { ...allReach(), kill_switch: false } }));
  check("keystone kill_switch probe fail → absent", noSentry.armed.kill_switch === "absent");
  check("keystone probe failure refuses (no reduced mode)", noSentry.proceed === false && noSentry.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "guardrail:kill_switch"));

  // Holdout keystone probe fails → refuse.
  const noHoldout = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ reachable: { ...allReach(), holdout: false } }));
  check("keystone holdout probe failure refuses", noHoldout.proceed === false && noHoldout.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "guardrail:holdout"));

  // Floor assertion failure → refuse.
  const noFloor = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ floor: { ...okFloor, no_execute: false } }));
  check("floor assertion failure refuses", noFloor.proceed === false && noFloor.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "floor:no_execute"));

  // ---- FAFF-379: worktree_isolation is a CHECKED floor entry (real probe); the ----
  // other two are STATIC invariants. Synthetic-floor refuse + floor_detail passthrough
  // + banner mode tokens + the pure checkWorktreeIsolation probe over an injected fsq.
  const noWtFloor = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({ floor: { ...okFloor, worktree_isolation: false } }));
  check("worktree_isolation floor failure refuses with its named gate",
    noWtFloor.proceed === false && noWtFloor.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "floor:worktree_isolation"));
  check("floor refusal without floor_detail keeps the generic message",
    /does not hold/.test(noWtFloor.refusals.find((r) => r.gate === "floor:worktree_isolation").detail));
  // floor_detail passthrough: a supplied per-key detail becomes the refusal detail verbatim.
  const wtDetail = "worktree root '/x/wt' is inside the repo working tree — synthetic";
  const detailFloor = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    floor: { ...okFloor, worktree_isolation: false }, floor_detail: { worktree_isolation: wtDetail },
  }));
  check("floor_detail passthrough: refusal detail equals the supplied string",
    detailFloor.refusals.find((r) => r.gate === "floor:worktree_isolation").detail === wtDetail);
  // Banner: worktree-isolation renders `checked`, the two statics render `static`.
  check("banner floor line marks worktree-isolation checked and the others static",
    /worktree-isolation ✓ checked/.test(happy.banner)
    && /no-execute ✓ static/.test(happy.banner)
    && /autonomous-contract ✓ static/.test(happy.banner));

  // Direct checkWorktreeIsolation over a synthetic fsq (no real filesystem touched).
  const isoFsq = (existing, writableSet) => ({
    exists: (p) => existing.has(p),
    isDirectory: (p) => existing.has(p),        // every existing synthetic path is a dir unless overridden
    writable: (p) => writableSet.has(p),
    readEnviron: () => "",
  });
  const repoR = "/repo";
  const insideV = checkWorktreeIsolation("/repo/wt", repoR, isoFsq(new Set(["/repo"]), new Set(["/repo"])));
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: inside-repo root refuses", insideV.holds === false && /inside the repo/.test(insideV.detail));
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: repo root itself refuses",
    checkWorktreeIsolation("/repo", repoR, isoFsq(new Set(["/repo"]), new Set(["/repo"]))).holds === false);
  // segment-aware: a sibling sharing a name prefix is NOT inside (bare startsWith would misfire).
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: sibling sharing a name prefix is outside",
    checkWorktreeIsolation("/repository/wt", repoR, isoFsq(new Set(["/repository"]), new Set(["/repository"]))).holds === true);
  const okV = checkWorktreeIsolation("/outside/wt", repoR, isoFsq(new Set(["/outside"]), new Set(["/outside"])));
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: writable outside root with nonexistent leaf holds", okV.holds === true && okV.detail === null);
  const roV = checkWorktreeIsolation("/outside/wt", repoR, isoFsq(new Set(["/outside"]), new Set()));
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: non-writable ancestor refuses", roV.holds === false && /not writable/.test(roV.detail));
  const fileFsq = { exists: (p) => p === "/outside", isDirectory: () => false, writable: () => true, readEnviron: () => "" };
  const ndV = checkWorktreeIsolation("/outside/wt", repoR, fileFsq);
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: non-directory ancestor refuses", ndV.holds === false && /non-directory/.test(ndV.detail));
  const throwFsq = { exists: () => { throw new Error("boom"); }, isDirectory: () => true, writable: () => true, readEnviron: () => "" };
  const thrownV = checkWorktreeIsolation("/outside/wt", repoR, throwFsq);
  check("checkWorktreeIsolation: fsq throw is caught → fail-closed", thrownV.holds === false && /boom/.test(thrownV.detail));

  // Every derived armed state is in the closed vocabulary.
  check("armed states are in {live,degraded,absent}", LIGHTS_OUT_GUARDRAIL_IDS.every((id) => GUARDRAIL_STATES.has(happy.armed[id]) && GUARDRAIL_STATES.has(bare.armed[id])));

  // ---- Dial-coherence (FAFF-298) -----------------------------------------
  // The coherent default dial proceeds (folded into the happy path above too).
  check("coherent dial proceeds (no coherence refusals)",
    happy.proceed === true && !happy.refusals.some((r) => r.gate.startsWith("dial-coherence:")));

  // Rule (A) — a non-adversarial review occupant refuses with its named gate; every
  // basic precondition still passes so the ONLY refusal is the coherence one.
  const reckReview = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    dial: { ...coherentDial(), slots: { review: "faffter-noon-review", spec_review: "faffter-dark-spec-review" } },
  }));
  check("Rule A: non-adversarial review refuses",
    reckReview.proceed === false && reckReview.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:adversarial-review"));
  check("Rule A: review refusal is the only refusal (basic checks all pass)",
    reckReview.refusals.length === 1);

  // Rule (A) — a non-adversarial spec_review occupant refuses with its named gate.
  const reckSpecReview = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    dial: { ...coherentDial(), slots: { review: "faffter-dark-adversarial-review", spec_review: "faffter-noon-spec-review" } },
  }));
  check("Rule A: non-adversarial spec_review refuses",
    reckSpecReview.proceed === false && reckSpecReview.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:adversarial-spec-review"));

  // Rule (B) — gates.fallback = advisory refuses with its named gate.
  const reckGates = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    dial: { ...coherentDial(), gates_fallback: "advisory" },
  }));
  check("Rule B: advisory gates.fallback refuses",
    reckGates.proceed === false && reckGates.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:gates-fallback"));

  // Edge: an unrecognised gates.fallback token refuses fail-closed (inequality).
  const reckGatesTypo = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    dial: { ...coherentDial(), gates_fallback: "fail-clsoed" },
  }));
  check("Edge: unrecognised gates.fallback token refuses fail-closed",
    reckGatesTypo.refusals.some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:gates-fallback"));

  // Edge: null / unknown occupant names refuse fail-closed, not a silent pass.
  check("Edge: null review occupant refuses fail-closed",
    dialCoherence({ slots: { review: null, spec_review: "faffter-dark-spec-review" }, gates_fallback: "fail-closed" })
      .some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:adversarial-review"));
  check("Edge: unknown (bespoke) review occupant refuses fail-closed",
    dialCoherence({ slots: { review: "my-custom-reviewer", spec_review: "faffter-dark-spec-review" }, gates_fallback: "fail-closed" })
      .some((r) => r.gate === "dial-coherence:adversarial-review"));

  // isAdversarial classifier: false for null/unknown, true for an allowlisted name.
  check("isAdversarial(null) is false", isAdversarial(null, ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_OCCUPANTS) === false);
  check("isAdversarial(unknown) is false", isAdversarial("nope", ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_OCCUPANTS) === false);
  check("isAdversarial(allowlisted) is true", isAdversarial("faffter-dark-adversarial-review", ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_OCCUPANTS) === true);

  // FAFF-377: VETTED_RECIPES is empty, so a recipe name alone never short-circuits —
  // an otherwise-reckless dial still yields refusals even with a recognised recipe name.
  check("named recipe does NOT short-circuit a reckless dial",
    dialCoherence({ recipe: "mature-prod", slots: { review: "faffter-noon-review", spec_review: "faffter-noon-spec-review" }, gates_fallback: "advisory" }).length > 0);
  const vettedProceed = lightsOutPreflight(armedProbes({
    dial: { level: "L4", recipe: "mature-prod", slots: { review: "faffter-dark-adversarial-review", spec_review: "faffter-dark-spec-review" }, gates_fallback: "fail-closed" },
  }));
  check("recipe name + a coherent dial proceeds (via Rules A+B, not the name)", vettedProceed.proceed === true);

  // Edge: a non-vetted recipe string falls THROUGH to the standalone rules (no auto-pass).
  check("non-vetted recipe falls through to the standalone rules",
    dialCoherence({ recipe: "made-up-recipe", slots: { review: "faffter-noon-review", spec_review: "faffter-noon-spec-review" }, gates_fallback: "advisory" }).length > 0);

  // FAFF-377 trip-wire: VETTED_RECIPES must stay empty until FAFF-18 satisfies the
  // re-population contract (schema guarantees-by-construction, or verify-not-trust).
  check("VETTED_RECIPES empty until FAFF-18", VETTED_RECIPES.size === 0);

  // Assertion: every coherence refusal carries a `dial-coherence:` gate and a non-empty detail.
  const allCoherenceRefusals = [...reckReview.refusals, ...reckSpecReview.refusals, ...reckGates.refusals]
    .filter((r) => r.gate.startsWith("dial-coherence:"));
  check("coherence refusals are greppable + have non-empty detail",
    allCoherenceRefusals.length >= 3 && allCoherenceRefusals.every((r) => /^dial-coherence:/.test(r.gate) && typeof r.detail === "string" && r.detail.length > 0));

  // preflight with NO dial supplied skips coherence (internal callers only; the
  // wrapper always supplies one) — proves the guard, not a silent coherence pass.

// ===========================================================================
// === region:governance — runcheck — verify a beep-boop run dispatched its queue ===
// ===========================================================================
// Vocabulary: "unit" — the governance core's name for the thing a run admits and
// resolves. In faff-the-factory's dialect a unit is an issue id; persisted formats
// keep their field names (see the compat notes at each definition site).
//
// TERMINAL_STATES — the outcome vocabulary of the run ledger: the terminal states a
// unit's recorded outcome must resolve to. Ledger `admitted[]` entries and `outcomes{}`
// keys are unit keys:
// "issue" — the unit key (compat dialect; rename deferred to extraction schema-v2)

const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");
const { overlayHeartbeat, readHeartbeatFile } = require("./heartbeat");
const { activeProfile, DELIVERY_PROFILE } = require("./governance-profile");
const { findRoot, latestRunDir, readLedger, RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS_DEFAULT } = require("./shared-infra");

// FAFF-362: TERMINAL_STATES stays exported (governance-check.js/disposition.js
// reuse it directly as a Set) but is now DERIVED from the active-by-default
// delivery profile rather than an independent literal — same 6 values,
// byte-identical, single-sourced in governance-profile.js's DELIVERY_PROFILE.
const TERMINAL_STATES = new Set(DELIVERY_PROFILE.terminal_states);

// Pure audit over a parsed ledger object (FAFF-205): the completeness core,
// decoupled from disk so the gate (which already holds the ledger) and the
// selftest can both drive it. `run_id` falls back to the caller-supplied label.
// FAFF-362: `profile` is a trailing defaulted parameter (mirrors the existing
// nowFn/getFn injectable-seam pattern) — the default resolves DELIVERY_PROFILE
// (byte-identical), an explicit profile (e.g. SECOND_PROFILE) drives a different
// dialect's terminal-state vocabulary with no other code path change.
function auditLedger(data, label, profile = activeProfile()) {
  const admitted = [...new Set(data.admitted ?? [])];
  const outcomes = data.outcomes ?? {};
  if (typeof outcomes !== "object" || Array.isArray(outcomes)) throw new Error("outcomes must be an object");
  const undispatched = admitted.filter((i) => !(i in outcomes));
  const validStates = new Set(profile.terminal_states);
  // FAFF-554: outcomes[issue] MUST be a terminal-state string — rich per-issue detail
  // belongs in the additive outcome_details sidecar (never read here; it is not
  // `outcomes`, so it never enters this invariant). A non-string value (e.g. a run
  // author's `{ state, merged_head, ... }` detail object) is still invalid — that
  // authoring shape is rejected on purpose (FAFF-554 keeps option (a): no schema
  // widening) — but the diagnostic now names the sidecar instead of stringifying the
  // object to the useless "[object Object]".
  const invalid = [...new Set(Object.entries(outcomes)
    .map(([i, s]) => {
      if (typeof s !== "string") {
        return `${i}=<non-string outcome; record rich detail in outcome_details, keep outcomes[${i}] a terminal-state string>`;
      }
      return validStates.has(s) ? null : `${i}=${s}`;
    })
    .filter((s) => s !== null))].sort();
  return {
    run_id: data.run_id ?? label,
    admitted, undispatched, invalid_outcomes: invalid,
    clean: undispatched.length === 0 && invalid.length === 0,
  };
}

function auditRun(runDir) {
  const result = auditLedger(readLedger(runDir), path.basename(runDir));
  result.run_dir = runDir;
  return result;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// FAFF-205 — ownership + liveness gate for the runcheck Stop hook.
//
// The Stop hook fires on EVERY session's turn-end and audits the newest run
// ledger globally. A parallel beep-boop drain's legitimately in-flight ledger
// (admitted, no terminal outcome yet) looks identical to an abandoned queue, so
// the hook false-blocks an unrelated session. The gate: HARD-BLOCK only for the
// session that OWNS the run (env/session match) or an explicit --recover; a foreign
// run that a live owner is draining → silent; a foreign run that looks abandoned →
// a non-blocking WARN, never a hard block (FAFF-235 — a non-owner is never trapped).
//
// Pure-function CLI invariant: liveness is on-disk owner-emitted state — owner.status
// + owner.last_heartbeat on the ledger — never a tracker/network probe. Liveness is
// HEARTBEAT-ONLY (FAFF-233): the recorded owner.pid is NOT consulted, because the
// beep-boop worker pid rolls and a dead recorded pid is no evidence of death while
// heartbeats still arrive.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// FAFF-362: RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS_DEFAULT now lives in shared-infra.js (single
// source, imported above) and is re-exported below unchanged for every existing
// consumer (sentry.js) — see shared-infra.js's comment for why.

function heartbeatStaleSecs(env) {
  const raw = (env || process.env).FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS;
  const n = raw == null ? NaN : Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? n : RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS_DEFAULT;
}

// Does the current session OWN the resolved run? Two signal-agnostic sources
// (the §7 assumption is de-risked by implementing both): the FAFF_RUN_DIR env
// pointer matched against the resolved dir, OR the owner.session_id on the ledger
// matched against FAFF_SESSION_ID. Either match proves ownership. An interactive
// session sets neither, so it can never be mistaken for a foreign run's owner.
function runIsOwned(ledger, runDir, env) {
  const e = env || process.env;
  if (e.FAFF_RUN_DIR && runDir && path.resolve(e.FAFF_RUN_DIR) === path.resolve(runDir)) return true;
  const owner = ledger && ledger.owner;
  if (owner && owner.session_id && e.FAFF_SESSION_ID && owner.session_id === e.FAFF_SESSION_ID) return true;
  return false;
}

// FAFF-690 (F4): the CONTENT-INDEPENDENT ownership clause of runIsOwned, extracted so it works with
// NO ledger object — the only ownership signal available when the ledger fails to PARSE (there is no
// parsed `owner.session_id` to match). Used at the hook-entry readLedger catch, where a corrupt
// ledger this session provably owns must fail closed (block) rather than silently return success.
function ownedByEnvPointer(runDir, env) {
  const e = env || process.env;
  return !!(e.FAFF_RUN_DIR && runDir && path.resolve(e.FAFF_RUN_DIR) === path.resolve(runDir));
}

// FAFF-690 (F4): the hard-block reason when an OWNED run's ledger is malformed/unreadable — the
// completion backstop cannot confirm the queue drained, so it fails closed instead of exiting silent.
function malformedOwnedReason(runDir) {
  return `faff runcheck: the owned run ledger at ${runDir} is malformed/unreadable — the completion backstop cannot confirm the build queue drained; fix or remove the ledger before stopping (owned session, fail-closed).`;
}

// Is the run still HELD by a live owner? Contract = owner.status "running" + a
// heartbeat fresher than STALE_SECS. Absent owner / non-running / stale / missing
// / unparseable heartbeat ⇒ NOT held (fail-safe toward firing). nowMs/env are
// injectable so the selftest drives this as a pure function.
//
// FAFF-233: liveness is HEARTBEAT-ONLY. The recorded owner.pid is NOT consulted —
// the beep-boop worker pid rolls between issues (observed 35795→36342), so a dead
// `kill -0` on the *recorded* pid is no evidence the run is gone while heartbeats
// are still arriving. A fresh heartbeat means something live is writing it; that
// wins. (The old dead-pid corroborator could only ever fire on an already-fresh
// heartbeat — the stale-check returns first — so it never shortened the window, it
// only wrongly flipped live runs to not-held. Removed.)
function runIsHeld(ledger, nowMs, env) {
  const owner = ledger && ledger.owner;
  if (!owner) return false;                         // legacy/unowned ledger
  if (owner.status !== "running") return false;     // owner exited
  const t = Date.parse(owner.last_heartbeat);
  if (!Number.isFinite(t)) return false;            // missing/unparseable → not held
  const ageSecs = (nowMs - t) / 1000;
  if (ageSecs > heartbeatStaleSecs(env)) return false; // stale → presumed gone
  return true;                                       // running + fresh heartbeat → held (pid not consulted)
}

function resolveRunDir(arg) {
  if (arg) return fs.existsSync(path.join(arg, "run-ledger.json")) ? arg : null;
  return latestRunDir(findRoot());
}

// The block-reason text (shared by the hook and the selftest expectation).
function runcheckReason(result) {
  return (
    `faff runcheck: the latest beep-boop run (${result.run_id}) has ` +
    `${result.undispatched.length} admitted issue(s) with no terminal outcome: ` +
    `${result.undispatched.join(", ")}. These were admitted to the build queue but never ` +
    `dispatched — that is a deferred queue, not a complete run. Dispatch them (or genuinely ` +
    `park them under a valid category) before stopping.`
  );
}

// Pure decision for the Stop hook (FAFF-205): given a parsed ledger, the resolved
// run dir, the wall clock, the env, and opts, decide what the hook emits.
// Returns { block, warn, reason?, owned, held }. Drives both the live hook and the
// selftest without touching the filesystem.
//
// FAFF-235: a NON-OWNING session is never HARD-BLOCKED by another run's
// incompleteness — the Stop hook fires in every session/worktree, so a foreign
// run's undispatched work must not make an unrelated session un-exitable. Such a
// session gets at most a non-blocking WARN. Only the OWNING session (env/session
// match) — or an explicit human `--recover` — hard-blocks on undispatched work.
// This holds even if the liveness check ever misfires (defence in depth over RC1).
function runcheckHookDecision(ledger, runDir, nowMs, env, opts) {
  const recover = !!(opts && opts.recover);
  let result;
  try { result = auditLedger(ledger, ledger.run_id ?? path.basename(runDir || "")); }
  catch {
    // FAFF-690 (F4): the object PARSED but auditLedger threw (e.g. outcomes non-object). Both
    // runIsOwned clauses are usable here (the object is present). An OWNED run whose ledger cannot be
    // audited fails CLOSED — the backstop cannot confirm the queue drained. A foreign/ownership-
    // unprovable run stays silent, byte-identical to before (no non-owner can be hard-blocked here).
    if (runIsOwned(ledger, runDir, env)) return { block: true, warn: false, reason: malformedOwnedReason(runDir), owned: true, held: false };
    return { block: false, warn: false, owned: false, held: false };
  }
  const owned = runIsOwned(ledger, runDir, env);
  const held = owned ? false : runIsHeld(ledger, nowMs, env);
  // Foreign AND a live owner is draining it → stay silent (FAFF-205).
  if (held) return { block: false, warn: false, owned, held: true };
  // No undispatched work → nothing to say.
  if (!result.undispatched.length) return { block: false, warn: false, owned, held: false };
  // Undispatched work + not held: the owning session (backstop) or a deliberate
  // --recover hard-blocks; any other (foreign) session only warns, never blocks.
  if (owned || recover) return { block: true, warn: false, reason: runcheckReason(result), owned, held: false };
  return { block: false, warn: true, reason: runcheckReason(result), owned, held: false };
}

const { parseArgs, usageError } = require("./argv");
// --root is declared (accepted-and-ignored — runcheck resolves its run-dir from the
// positional) so probeServes's `runcheck --hook --root <probeRoot>` never trips unknown-flag.
const RUNCHECK_SPEC = {
  flags: { "--selftest": { arity: 0 }, "--hook": { arity: 0 }, "--json": { arity: 0 }, "--recover": { arity: 0 }, "--root": { arity: 1 } },
  positionals: { min: 0, max: 1, name: "run-dir" },
};

function cmdRuncheck(args) {
  if (args.includes("--selftest")) return runcheckSelftest();
  const parsed = parseArgs(args, RUNCHECK_SPEC);
  if (parsed.errors.length) return usageError(parsed.errors, "usage: faff runcheck [RUN_DIR] [--hook] [--recover] [--json]");
  const hook = !!parsed.values["--hook"];
  const asJson = !!parsed.values["--json"];
  const positional = parsed.positionals;
  // FAFF-578: defence in depth — resolution no longer throws on fs churn
  // (latestRunDir absorbs it), but a Stop hook that fires at every turn-end must
  // never crash on filesystem churn. Hook mode: silent, as if no run exists
  // (parity with the parse-error → silent rule below). CLI mode: loud fault
  // (parity with the missing/malformed-ledger handling below).
  let runDir;
  try {
    runDir = resolveRunDir(positional[0]);
  } catch (e) {
    if (hook) return 0;
    process.stderr.write(`runcheck: run-dir resolution failed: ${e.message}\n`);
    return 2;
  }

  if (hook) {
    if (!runDir) return 0;
    let ledger;
    try { ledger = readLedger(runDir); }
    catch {
      // FAFF-690 (F4): readLedger does JSON.parse(readFileSync(...)), so BOTH a parse error and an
      // unreadable file throw here — there is NO ledger object, so ownership can only be established
      // by the content-independent FAFF_RUN_DIR env pointer. An OWNED corrupt ledger hard-blocks (the
      // block PAYLOAD on stdout + exit 0 is the Stop-hook block mechanism, parity with the block path
      // below); a foreign/unprovable one stays silent, byte-identical to before.
      if (ownedByEnvPointer(runDir, process.env)) {
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ decision: "block", reason: malformedOwnedReason(runDir) }));
        return 0;
      }
      return 0; // foreign/unprovable (no env pointer) → silent (unchanged)
    }
    // FAFF-355: overlay the dedicated heartbeat file over owner.last_heartbeat BEFORE
    // the pure decision runs — the decision fn (runcheckHookDecision → runIsHeld)
    // stays filesystem-free; this is the one read of the file for this seam.
    overlayHeartbeat(ledger, readHeartbeatFile(runDir));
    const recover = !!parsed.values["--recover"];
    const decision = runcheckHookDecision(ledger, runDir, Date.now(), process.env, { recover });
    if (decision.block) console.log(JSON.stringify({ decision: "block", reason: decision.reason }));
    // FAFF-235: foreign + not-held → a one-line, NON-BLOCKING notice on stderr (never the
    // block payload), so a genuinely-abandoned foreign run is still surfaced without making
    // an unrelated session un-exitable.
    else if (decision.warn) process.stderr.write(`[warn] ${decision.reason}\n`);
    return 0;
  }

  if (!runDir) { process.stderr.write("runcheck: no .faff/runs/*/run-ledger.json found\n"); return 2; }
  let result;
  try {
    result = auditRun(runDir);
  } catch (e) {
    process.stderr.write(`runcheck: missing or malformed ledger in ${runDir}: ${e.message}\n`);
    return 2;
  }

  if (asJson) {
    console.log(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
  } else {
    console.log(`run:       ${result.run_id}`);
    console.log(`admitted:  ${result.admitted.length}`);
    if (result.invalid_outcomes.length) console.log(`INVALID outcomes: ${result.invalid_outcomes.join(", ")}`);
    if (result.undispatched.length) {
      console.log(`UNDISPATCHED (${result.undispatched.length}): ${result.undispatched.join(", ")}`);
      console.log("→ run is NOT complete: dispatch these or park them under a valid category.");
    } else {
      console.log("clean: every admitted issue reached a terminal outcome.");
    }
  }
  if (result.undispatched.length) return 3;
  if (result.invalid_outcomes.length) return 2;
  return 0;
}

// Selftest (FAFF-205) — drives the Stop-hook gate as a pure function over
// (ledger, runDir, env-owned?, now) tuples. A fixed NOW anchors the heartbeat
// ages so the held/abandoned branches are deterministic. Covers both branches the
// AC requires plus the legacy and ownership cases.
const RUNCHECK_NOW = Date.parse("2026-06-22T16:00:00Z");
const RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR = "/runs/RUN-LIVE";
function hbAgo(secs) { return new Date(RUNCHECK_NOW - secs * 1000).toISOString(); }

// [name, ledger, env, wantBlock, wantWarn, opts?, heartbeatFile?]
// FAFF-235 contract change: foreign (not-owned) + not-held + undispatched is now a
// non-blocking WARN, not a block. Only OWNED or --recover hard-blocks. FAFF-233:
// liveness is heartbeat-only, so a fresh heartbeat is held even with a dead recorded pid.
// FAFF-355: an optional trailing `heartbeatFile` column (ISO string | undefined) is
// overlaid onto a CLONE of the fixture ledger before the decision runs — undefined on
// every pre-existing case preserves ledger-field-only behaviour byte-for-byte; the
// new cases below exercise the file/field interaction the overlay is for.
const RUNCHECK_SELFTEST_CASES = [
  ["owned + undispatched → block (backstop preserved)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    { FAFF_RUN_DIR: RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR }, true, false],
  ["owned + clean queue → silent",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: { X: "shipped" }, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    { FAFF_RUN_DIR: RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR }, false, false],
  ["not-owned + held (running, fresh heartbeat) → silent (FAFF-205)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false],
  ["FAFF-233: not-owned + fresh heartbeat + DEAD recorded pid → held/silent (pid not consulted)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", pid: 2147483646, last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false],
  ["FAFF-235: not-owned + stale heartbeat + undispatched → WARN, not block (abandoned still surfaced)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(1000) } },
    {}, false, true],
  ["FAFF-235: not-owned + status:done + undispatched → WARN, not block",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "done", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, true],
  ["FAFF-235: legacy ledger (no owner) + undispatched → WARN, not block (no foreign hard-block)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {} },
    {}, false, true],
  ["not-owned + held + clean queue → silent",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: { X: "shipped" }, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false],
  ["FAFF-235: not-owned + unparseable heartbeat + undispatched → WARN, not block",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: "not-a-date" } },
    {}, false, true],
  ["owned via session_id fallback + undispatched → block (backstop, env-pointer absent)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", session_id: "S1", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    { FAFF_SESSION_ID: "S1" }, true, false],
  ["FAFF-235: custom STALE_SECS shrinks the window (foreign) → WARN, not block",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(120) } },
    { FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS: "60" }, false, true],
  ["FAFF-235: --recover on a foreign not-held undispatched run → block (deliberate human recovery)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(1000) } },
    {}, true, false, { recover: true }],
  ["FAFF-235: --recover + clean queue → silent (nothing to recover)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: { X: "shipped" }, owner: { status: "done", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(1000) } },
    {}, false, false, { recover: true }],
  ["FAFF-355: not-owned + fresh heartbeat FILE (stale field) + undispatched → held/silent (file wins)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(1000) } },
    {}, false, false, undefined, hbAgo(10)],
  ["FAFF-355: not-owned + no file + fresh field + undispatched → held/silent (ledger-field fallback)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false, undefined, null],
  ["FAFF-355: not-owned + both file and field stale + undispatched → WARN, not block",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(1000) } },
    {}, false, true, undefined, hbAgo(1000)],
  ["FAFF-355: not-owned + unparseable file + fresh field + undispatched → held/silent (field fallback)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: {}, owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false, undefined, "not-a-date"],
  // FAFF-690 (F4): a MALFORMED ledger (outcomes a non-object → auditLedger throws) this session OWNS
  // fails CLOSED (block); a foreign malformed ledger stays silent (foreign safety byte-identical).
  ["FAFF-690: owned (env-pointer) + malformed ledger (outcomes non-object) → block (fail-closed)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: [], owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    { FAFF_RUN_DIR: RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR }, true, false],
  ["FAFF-690: foreign + malformed ledger (outcomes non-object) → silent (no foreign hard-block)",
    { run_id: "R", admitted: ["X"], outcomes: [], owner: { status: "running", last_heartbeat: hbAgo(10) } },
    {}, false, false],
];

function runcheckSelftest() {
  let fail = 0;
  for (const [name, ledger, env, wantBlock, wantWarn, opts, heartbeatFile] of RUNCHECK_SELFTEST_CASES) {
    // Clone before overlay — these fixtures are shared array literals and overlayHeartbeat
    // mutates owner.last_heartbeat in place; a clone keeps each case isolated + rerunnable.
    const cloned = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(ledger));
    overlayHeartbeat(cloned, heartbeatFile === undefined ? null : heartbeatFile);
    const d = runcheckHookDecision(cloned, RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR, RUNCHECK_NOW, env, opts);
    const ok = d.block === wantBlock && (d.warn || false) === (wantWarn || false);
    if (!ok) fail++;
    console.log(`${ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL"} ${name} → block=${d.block} warn=${d.warn || false} (want block=${wantBlock} warn=${wantWarn || false})`);
  }
  console.log(`\nRESULT: ${fail ? "FAIL" : "PASS"} (${RUNCHECK_SELFTEST_CASES.length} cases, ${fail} failed)`);
  return fail ? 1 : 0;
}


module.exports = { RUNCHECK_NOW, RUNCHECK_RUN_DIR, RUNCHECK_SELFTEST_CASES, RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS_DEFAULT, TERMINAL_STATES, auditLedger, auditRun, cmdRuncheck, hbAgo, heartbeatStaleSecs, malformedOwnedReason, ownedByEnvPointer, resolveRunDir, runIsHeld, runIsOwned, runcheckHookDecision, runcheckReason, runcheckSelftest };

# Harden claimStoreCore: clock-skew-safe staleness and TOCTOU-closed reclaim

> Spec: faffter-dark-nlspec · 2026-08-25 · interactive · claude-code/unknown · confidence: high. Full spec on Linear FAFF-906.

This spec covers FAFF-906, a Linear ticket in the Faff team tracker ("Harden the shared claim-store staleness/reclaim primitive"). It is written for the build agent that implements the change and for a human reviewer checking the design before merge. The target file is `plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/bundle.js`.

## 1. WHY

The shared claim mutex (`claimStoreCore`, `bundle.js`, lines roughly 693 to 818) already gets the hard part right: every ref move it makes is either a non-force create (git rejects a second push to a ref that already exists) or a `--force-with-lease` push fenced to the exact sha the caller last read. That fencing is a genuine compare-and-swap. What it does not get right is upstream of the CAS: the decision of *whether to attempt a reclaim at all* rests on comparing the reclaiming machine's `Date.now()` against a `last_heartbeat` string written by the holder's machine. Two machines' clocks are never guaranteed to agree, so a reader running fast can judge a live, heartbeating holder stale and win a reclaim it should have lost. The CAS then faithfully executes that wrong decision, because the CAS only proves "the ref hadn't moved since I read it," not "the holder is actually dead."

**Problem statement.** `recoveryClaimStore` and `buildClaimStore` both delegate their staleness verdict to `claimStoreCore.reclaimIfStale`, which currently feeds each binding's `stalePredicate` a bare `Date.now()`. A reader whose clock runs ahead of the holder's can misjudge a live holder as stale and reclaim it, opening a double-drain: two executors believing they each own the same recovery segment or the same build. This spec narrows that gap at the one shared call site with a best-effort, operator-configurable tolerance margin — skew beyond the configured tolerance remains unmitigated, exactly as it is today — and separately settles whether the reclaim's read-then-act sequence has an open TOCTOU window at all, since a close read of the existing `--force-with-lease` fencing and its selftest suggests it may already be closed.

**Design principles.**

**The fix lives at exactly one call site.** `runIsHeld` (`runcheck.js`) is shared by non-claim-store consumers (the Stop-hook gate, `sentry.js`) for same-process liveness checks that have nothing to do with cross-machine claims. The ticket's scope pins changes to `bundle.js`, so this spec never edits `runcheck.js` or `runIsHeld`'s signature. The tolerance is applied to the `nowMs` value `reclaimIfStale` passes into `spec.stalePredicate`, not inside any predicate function.

**The tolerance is a per-predicate property, not a blanket call-site behaviour.** Round 1 of this spec applied the skew tolerance unconditionally, to every binding's `stalePredicate`, regardless of whether that predicate's reclaim decision has any cross-machine comparison to correct. That is wasteful in one direction: a predicate whose reclaim carries no destructive blast radius still pays the full tolerance as pure delay, for zero additional safety. `reclaimIfStale` now reads an explicit `spec.applySkewTolerance` flag on each binding and only widens the window when the binding says it needs it (see WHAT and HOW).

**A verdict that turns out wrong must still fail safe.** Even after this fix, a `stalePredicate` misjudgment is possible in principle (skew larger than the tolerance, a genuinely wedged process that keeps writing heartbeats). The system's actual safety net for that case is `confirmHead`, called by the true holder immediately before its first irreversible write. Nothing in this spec is allowed to weaken that pin, and the spec treats it as the backstop, not a wrong-verdict fix.

**The tolerance is a best-effort mitigation, not a guarantee.** A fixed margin only compensates for skew up to its own value. Skew beyond the configured tolerance is unmitigated by this fix, exactly as it was before this spec: a reader whose clock runs more than `FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS` ahead of the holder's can still misjudge a live, heartbeating holder as stale. This spec does not claim to close the clock-skew problem outright; it narrows the window in which skew produces a wrong verdict and leans on two things that already exist to bound the residual risk: `confirmHead`'s CAS (a wrong verdict costs a wasted reclaim attempt, never a double-drain — see the principle above) and the tolerance's own operator override (an environment with drift worse than the 60-second default is not stuck with it; see WHAT and the Design decision rationale).

## 2. Out of scope

- **`landingClaimStore` binding.** FAFF-842 adds this binding on its own branch. Because the fix in this spec is applied inside `claimStoreCore.reclaimIfStale` itself (the shared call site every binding routes through), FAFF-842's binding inherits both the clock-skew tolerance and the CAS guarantee automatically once it rebases onto this change, with no code of its own needed for either property — an undeclared `applySkewTolerance` field defaults to `true`, so `landingClaimStore` gets the tolerance for free unless a future spec deliberately opts it out. Extension point: `plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/bundle.js`, wherever FAFF-842 defines `landingClaimStore` alongside `recoveryClaimStore` and `buildClaimStore`.
- **`runIsHeld` / `runcheck.js` changes.** Out of scope per the ticket; `runIsHeld` is shared with non-claim-store consumers and its cross-cutting behaviour must not shift. Extension point: none needed; the call-site fix in `reclaimIfStale` covers every current and future `stalePredicate` that shares its shape.
- **A monotonic heartbeat counter/generation number (the ticket's "preferred" fix direction).** Rejected here, not deferred: see design decision rationale for why the margin-based fix is chosen instead. Extension point: if a future ticket wants to add a counter, it changes `claim.json`'s shape (a wire-format change this ticket's scope explicitly forbids) and the holder-side heartbeat writer (`heartbeat.js`), not `claimStoreCore`.
- **A `.faffrc.yaml` config key for the skew tolerance.** The tolerance is env-var-only (`FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS`), mirroring `FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS`, which also has no config-file counterpart. Extension point: `plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/config.js`'s `CANONICAL_CONFIG`, if a future ticket decides operators need to set it per-repo rather than per-invocation.

## 3. What changes

Two additions, both scoped entirely inside `bundle.js`, plus one intentional non-change with a documented rationale.

**New helper**, placed beside `resolveClaimTtlHours` (which already follows the identical env-parse-with-fallback shape):

```
CONSTANT CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS_DEFAULT = 60

FUNCTION resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs(env):
  raw = env.FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS
  IF raw is set and parses to a finite number >= 0:
    RETURN that number
  RETURN CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS_DEFAULT
```

**New spec field: `applySkewTolerance`** (optional Boolean on the object each binding passes to `claimStoreCore`, alongside the existing `refName` / `buildClaim` / `commitMessage` / `stalePredicate` / `name`). **`**Chosen:**` (round 3 rename)** — round 2 named this field `crossBox` and defined it as "is this predicate a cross-machine comparison." The round-2 architectural review correctly caught that this name does not match the field's actual decision criterion: the Design decision rationale for `recoveryClaimStore`'s opt-out explicitly does NOT argue from machine topology ("The reasoning does not depend on whether `recoveryClaimStore`'s underlying git-remote ref namespace can, in principle, be read from a different machine") — it argues from what a wrong verdict costs (blast radius, backstopped or not by `confirmHead`). A name describing reachability, next to a rationale that disclaims reachability as the criterion, is a real defect: a future binding author reading only the field name would apply the wrong test. `applySkewTolerance` names the field for what it actually gates — whether `reclaimIfStale` pays the tolerance delay for this binding's reclaim decision — with no claim about topology. `undefined` and `true` both mean "pay the tolerance"; `false` means "zero tolerance, always." The default (an undeclared `applySkewTolerance`) stays `true`, not `false`: a future binding that forgets to declare it still gets the tolerance, rather than silently reclaiming with zero grace period. Only a binding that explicitly opts OUT loses the tolerance — see `recoveryClaimStore` below and the Design decision rationale for the actual criterion (wrong-verdict cost, not reachability).

**Changed call site**, inside `claimStoreCore.reclaimIfStale` (currently line 776):

```
# before
held = spec.stalePredicate(existing.claim, Date.now(), env)

# after
# The tolerance corrects for the READING (reclaiming) machine's clock running ahead of the
# holder's by up to `toleranceSecs`. It does NOT correct skew in the other direction (holder's
# clock ahead of reader's — that direction already biases toward "held", the safe direction) and
# does NOT correct reader-ahead skew beyond `toleranceSecs`: a reader whose clock runs more than
# `toleranceSecs` ahead of the holder's still misjudges a live holder as stale. See WHY
# ("best-effort mitigation, not a guarantee") for the residual-risk argument.
toleranceSecs = spec.applySkewTolerance === false ? 0 : resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs(env)
skewedNowMs = Date.now() - toleranceSecs * 1000
held = spec.stalePredicate(existing.claim, skewedNowMs, env)
```

**Changed binding**, `recoveryClaimStore`'s spec object gains one field:

```
# before
{
  name: "git-remote-recovery-claim",
  refName: ...,
  buildClaim: ...,
  commitMessage: ...,
  stalePredicate: (claim, nowMs, env) => runIsHeld({ owner: claim.owner }, nowMs, env),
}

# after
{
  name: "git-remote-recovery-claim",
  refName: ...,
  buildClaim: ...,
  commitMessage: ...,
  stalePredicate: (claim, nowMs, env) => runIsHeld({ owner: claim.owner }, nowMs, env),  # unchanged
  // applySkewTolerance: false — NOT a claim that this ref namespace is same-box (it can be read
  // cross-box; see the recoveryClaimStore header comment). Set false because a wrong verdict here
  // costs one avoided-but-harmless resume attempt (confirmHead's CAS refuses the loser), while on
  // buildClaimStore/landingClaimStore a wrong verdict hands over live, destructive work — see
  // "Design decision rationale" in the attached spec (FAFF-906) for the full argument.
  applySkewTolerance: false,
}
```

`buildClaimStore`'s spec object gains no field — an undeclared `applySkewTolerance` already defaults to `true`, which is the behaviour Problem 1 needs for its cross-box row. That is the entire code change for Problem 1: one new field on one binding, one branch at the call site. Nothing else in `reclaimIfStale`, `recoveryClaimStore`, or `buildClaimStaleAware` changes shape or signature.

**`**Chosen:**` no change to `buildClaimStaleAware` itself.** `buildClaimStaleAware(root, claim, nowMs, env, deps)` keeps its exact current signature and body. Because `reclaimIfStale` is the only caller that feeds it a real `Date.now()`-derived `nowMs` (the `buildClaimSelftest` pure-predicate table calls it directly with a fixed test instant, bypassing `reclaimIfStale` entirely), skewing the value at the `reclaimIfStale` call site reaches `buildClaimStaleAware` through its `nowMs` parameter without touching the function. This is why the fix is a two-line change rather than three edits across three staleness paths.

**Problem 2, scoped down.** Read closely, `reclaimIfStale`'s reclaim write already uses `--force-with-lease=${ref}:${existing.sha}` (line 782): a git-server-side compare-and-swap keyed to the exact claim state read at the top of the function. Two reclaimers who both read the same stale sha and both attempt the CAS cannot both win; the loser's lease no longer matches and it re-reads to surface the winner (`lease-lost`), never a blind retry. The existing `pushX`/`pushY` selftest fixture (recoveryClaimStore block, lines roughly 1377 to 1386) already proves exactly this: two lease-matched CAS pushes against the same stale sha, exactly one succeeds. Its adjacent comment also explains why a naive test of two *sequential* `reclaimIfStale` calls cannot reproduce the race at all in a single-threaded harness: the second call's own read would see the first call's already-landed fresh claim and refuse via the `held` path before it ever reaches its own CAS. That is precisely why the existing test drives `pushClaimCommit` directly rather than `reclaimIfStale`, and it is the only way to construct this race without real concurrent processes.

**`**Chosen:**` Problem 2 requires no logic change to `reclaimIfStale`.** The compare-and-swap the ticket asks for already exists and is already covered by a passing selftest. What is missing is (a) the same coverage for the `buildClaimStore` ref namespace, which shares the code path but had no equivalent direct-CAS race test, and (b) a comment at `reclaimIfStale` stating the invariant outright, since this ticket is itself evidence the existing comments did not make it obvious enough. Both are additions, not fixes to broken logic.

## 4. How

### Reclaim staleness check, after the fix

```
PROCEDURE reclaim_if_stale(identity, ownerSnapshot, env):
  ref = spec.refName(identity)
  existing = read_claim_manifest(ref)
  IF existing is unreachable/missing/unreadable: (unchanged from today)

  toleranceSecs = spec.applySkewTolerance === false ? 0 : resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs(env)
  skewedNowMs = current_time_ms() - toleranceSecs * 1000
  held = spec.stalePredicate(existing.claim, skewedNowMs, env)
  IF held: RETURN { reclaimed: false, reason: "held", holder: existing.claim, sha: existing.sha }

  # everything below this line is UNCHANGED — the lease-matched CAS already fences
  # the write against existing.sha, so a concurrent reclaimer or a revived holder
  # (via confirmHead, on its own side) is already handled.
  newClaim = spec.buildClaim(identity, ownerSnapshot, existing.claim.claim_epoch + 1)
  push claim with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<existing.sha>`
  IF lease rejected: re-read, surface the new holder as "lease-lost"
  ELSE: RETURN { reclaimed: true, sha: newCommitSha, claim: newClaim }
```

**How the skew shift propagates to each existing predicate, row by row:**

- **`recoveryClaimStore`'s predicate** (`(claim, nowMs, env) => runIsHeld({ owner: claim.owner }, nowMs, env)`, `applySkewTolerance: false`): receives `skewedNowMs === Date.now()` — zero tolerance, unchanged from today's behaviour. `runIsHeld` computes `ageSecs = (nowMs - t) / 1000` against `heartbeatStaleSecs(env)` (900s default); with `toleranceSecs` pinned at 0, this row's verdict is byte-identical to round 1's *pre-fix* behaviour. See the Design decision rationale for why this row is deliberately excluded from Problem 1's fix rather than included by default.
- **`buildClaimStaleAware` Row 3 (cross-box)**: `buildClaimStore` does not declare `applySkewTolerance`, so it defaults to `true` and receives the skewed `nowMs` (identical shape to `recoveryClaimStore`'s predicate — `runIsHeld` on the frozen snapshot — but this binding's blast radius, per the Design decision rationale, justifies paying the tolerance). A smaller `nowMs` produces a smaller `ageSecs`, biasing toward "held" exactly when the reader's clock might be running ahead. This is the row Problem 1's fix actually targets.
- **`buildClaimStaleAware` Row 1 (`heartbeating: false`, TTL check)**: `claimVerdict(claim.claimed_at, new Date(nowMs).toISOString(), ttlHours)` also receives the skewed `nowMs` (the whole `buildClaimStore` binding shares one `applySkewTolerance` value — the flag is per-binding, not per-row, since all three rows are reached through the same `stalePredicate` function and the tolerance is applied once, upstream of it). **`**Chosen:**` no separate handling needed.** The default TTL is 6 hours (21,600 seconds); a 60-second tolerance widens that window by roughly 0.3 percent, which is immaterial and does not need its own test. `claim-verdict.js` already fails safe in the other direction too (any non-positive age reads as `live`), so this row was never fully clock-skew-blind; the fix simply extends the same conservative bias.
- **`buildClaimStaleAware` Row 2 (same-box, live heartbeat file)**: also receives the skewed `nowMs`, but Row 2 reads a heartbeat file off the *same* machine that is judging it, so there is no genuine cross-machine skew to correct. **`**Chosen:**` no test change needed.** The existing Row 2 selftest fixtures use ages of 10 seconds (fresh) and 5000 seconds (crashed), both far enough from any 900-second-plus-60-second boundary that a 60-second shift changes nothing about their verdicts. (Row 2 is a within-binding fast path, not a separate binding — it does not get its own `applySkewTolerance` flag; `buildClaimStore`'s single flag governs the call site upstream of all three rows, and Row 2's own machine-id/local-run-dir gate is what actually keeps it insensitive to the tolerance, not a flag value.)

**Recovery claims keep today's exact reclaim timing — `hcReclaimB` needs no change.** Because `recoveryClaimStore` now declares `applySkewTolerance: false`, `reclaimIfStale`'s `toleranceSecs` is pinned to 0 for every recovery-claim reclaim, so `skewedNowMs === Date.now()` exactly as it does on `main` today. The recovery-claim selftest's `hcReclaimB` fixture (lines roughly 1397 to 1407) manufactures a "B wrongly judges A's live claim stale" scenario — A's heartbeat baked 2 seconds in the past (`recentOwner`, line 1398), B reclaiming under an injected `FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS: "1"` window — specifically to prove `confirmHead`, not the staleness verdict, is the real safety net. With zero tolerance on this binding, that scenario is completely unaffected by this spec: B's `ageSecs` is still `2`, still `> 1` (the injected window), still reads as stale, and `hcReclaimB.reclaimed === true` keeps passing with no fixture edit. This is the payoff of round 2's per-predicate design over round 1's blanket one: round 1 needed to bump the fixture's baked age from 2000ms to 90000ms to keep it working around a tolerance that was never supposed to apply to this path in the first place; round 2 removes the need for that edit entirely, because the tolerance no longer reaches this predicate.

**QA regression guard — proving `recoveryClaimStore`'s zero tolerance, not the test, is what keeps `hcReclaimB` passing.** A fixture that "still passes with no edit" is only convincing if it can be shown to depend on the `applySkewTolerance: false` wiring rather than passing by coincidence (e.g. a bug that silently no-ops the whole `applySkewTolerance` mechanism would also leave this fixture green). Add a companion assertion, in the same test block, that deliberately runs the identical `hcReclaimB` scenario but with `recoveryClaimStore` swapped for a throwaway `claimStoreCore` binding whose `spec` is byte-identical except `applySkewTolerance` is *omitted* (so it falls back to the `true` default) — i.e. the round-1 (pre-fix-for-this-ticket) behaviour:

```
PROCEDURE test_hcReclaimB_would_fail_under_the_defaulted_applySkewTolerance():
  # Regression guard for the per-predicate design itself: proves applySkewTolerance:false is load-bearing,
  # not incidental. Same hcReclaimB scenario (2s-old heartbeat, injected 1s window), but run
  # against a claimStoreCore binding identical to recoveryClaimStore EXCEPT applySkewTolerance is omitted
  # (defaults to true) — i.e., what recoveryClaimStore's reclaim would compute if it inherited
  # the default cross-box tolerance instead of opting out.
  applySkewToleranceDefaultStore = claimStoreCore(rootB, "origin", { ...recoveryClaimStore's spec fields, applySkewTolerance: undefined })
  reclaim = applySkewToleranceDefaultStore.reclaimIfStale(hcIdentity, freshOwner("session-hc-b-defaulted"), wrongEnv)
  ASSERT reclaim.reclaimed === false, reason === "held"
  # effective age = 2s - 60s tolerance = negative → runIsHeld always reads held, so the SAME
  # scenario that must reclaim (proving zero-tolerance is exercised) would instead refuse if
  # applySkewTolerance defaulted through — a build that dropped `applySkewTolerance: false` from recoveryClaimStore's
  # spec object fails THIS assertion, not just a silently-still-green hcReclaimB.
```

This directly pairs with `hcReclaimB.reclaimed === true` (unmodified, above): one proves the zero-tolerance path reclaims when it should, the other proves the default-tolerance path would NOT reclaim under the identical scenario — so a build that accidentally leaves `applySkewTolerance: false` off `recoveryClaimStore` (or a build that ignores the flag entirely) fails at least one of the pair, rather than both coincidentally passing.

**`**Chosen:**` the `buildClaimStaleAware` pure-predicate table (lines roughly 1566 to 1608) needs no changes.** It calls `buildClaimStaleAware` directly with a fixed `now` value, never through `reclaimIfStale`, so it never sees the skew shift. Confirmed by tracing every call in that block.

**New selftest coverage for Problem 1** (added to the `buildClaimStore` selftest block, against the cross-box Row 3 path — `applySkewTolerance: true` is the default this predicate actually exercises now, so round 2 moves this coverage from `recoveryClaimStore`, which no longer receives any tolerance, to the binding that does):

```
PROCEDURE test_skew_tolerance_forgives_moderate_age():
  a cross-box build claim's frozen heartbeat baked 920 seconds in the past (900s window + 20s
    INTO the 60s tolerance zone — without the fix this would misclassify as stale)
  storeB.reclaimIfStale(...) via process.env (no injected window override)
  ASSERT reclaimed === false, reason === "held"

PROCEDURE test_skew_tolerance_is_not_a_permanent_deadlock():
  a cross-box build claim's frozen heartbeat baked 990 seconds in the past (900s window + 90s,
    PAST the 60s tolerance zone)
  storeB.reclaimIfStale(...) via process.env
  ASSERT reclaimed === true

PROCEDURE test_default_tolerance_is_pinned_at_60_seconds():
  # QA fix (round 2): the two tests above forgive a wide margin either side of the boundary and
  # would pass unchanged against a 59s or 61s default — neither pins the SPECIFIC value 60. This
  # test picks a heartbeat age that only reads "held" at exactly tolerance >= 60 (integer seconds),
  # so a build shipping a 59s default fails it.
  #
  # QA fix (round 3): the round-2 review correctly noted that reclaimIfStale calls Date.now() a
  # second time (inside the function), strictly after the fixture bakes its heartbeat timestamp —
  # call this gap delta (test-harness overhead; realistically single-digit to low-double-digit
  # milliseconds, generously bounded at 500ms even under a loaded CI runner). The chosen baked age
  # (959500ms) is safe against delta on BOTH sides of the boundary without needing to shrink it:
  #   - at tolerance=59 (buggy default): effective age = 959500 + delta - 59000 = 900500 + delta,
  #     which exceeds 900000 for ANY delta >= 0 -> reclaims (fails this assertion) unconditionally.
  #   - at tolerance=60 (real default):  effective age = 959500 + delta - 60000 = 899500 + delta,
  #     which stays <= 900000 (holds) for any delta <= 500ms -> passes this assertion.
  # So 959500ms is already delta-safe up to a 500ms harness gap; no different constant is needed.
  # This also requires the test to run under the REAL 900s heartbeatStaleSecs default, not
  # whatever happens to be in the ambient environment — explicitly ensure
  # FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS is UNSET for this test's env (delete it from the env object
  # passed to reclaimIfStale if present, do not merely rely on process.env's ambient state),
  # so a CI environment that happens to set that var cannot silently shift this test's oracle.
  #
  # QA fix (round 4, operator-directed): case A below only pins a LOWER bound — it fails a 59s
  # default but a 61s (or any larger) default also reads "held" and passes case A unchanged, so
  # on its own it never catches an over-generous default. Case B is the paired upper-bound: a
  # heartbeat baked 960500ms in the past (900s window + 60.5s) must RECLAIM at the real 60s
  # default (effective age 900.5s+delta > 900s) but must stay HELD at a 61s default (effective
  # age 899.5s+delta <= 900s for delta <= 500ms) — so a build shipping 61s fails case B instead
  # of passing silently. Case A and case B together pin the default to the half-open window
  # [59.5s, 60.5s), i.e. exactly 60 integer seconds; neither case alone does.
  (Case A — lower-bound pin)
  a cross-box build claim's frozen heartbeat baked 959500 milliseconds in the past
    (900s window + 59.5s — held iff toleranceSecs >= 59.5, i.e. only at the real 60s default;
    a 59s default computes effective age 900.5s+ > 900s and reclaims, failing this assertion)
  storeB.reclaimIfStale(...) via an env with FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS explicitly deleted/unset
    (no injected window override — exercises the DEFAULT, not an env override, since the default
    itself is what must be pinned; the explicit delete is the round-3 fix, not new behaviour)
  ASSERT reclaimed === false, reason === "held"

  (Case B — upper-bound pin, round-4 addition)
  a cross-box build claim's frozen heartbeat baked 960500 milliseconds in the past
    (900s window + 60.5s — reclaims iff toleranceSecs <= 60.5, i.e. only at the real 60s default
    or lower; a 61s default computes effective age 899.5s+ <= 900s and stays held, failing this
    assertion)
  storeB.reclaimIfStale(...) via the same env as case A (FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS unset,
    no injected window override)
  ASSERT reclaimed === true
```

**New selftest coverage for Problem 2** (mirrors the existing `pushX`/`pushY` recovery-claim lease-race fixture, added to `buildClaimSelftest`'s `buildClaimStore` block, against `refs/faff/build-claims/<issue>`):

```
PROCEDURE test_build_claim_lease_race():
  acquire a stale build claim, note its sha (existing.sha)
  build two competing claim objects (claimX, claimY)
  push both via pushClaimCommit with `--force-with-lease=<ref>:<existing.sha>`
  ASSERT exactly one push succeeds
```

**Comment addition**, at `reclaimIfStale`'s existing comment block (lines roughly 758 to 763): state explicitly that the `--force-with-lease` push is the answer to a check-then-act TOCTOU between two reclaimers, and that a wrong staleness verdict is a separate risk closed by `confirmHead`, not by the CAS. This is documentation, not a logic change, added so a future reader does not misdiagnose the same non-issue this ticket raised.

**Anti-pattern:** applying the skew tolerance inside `runIsHeld`, `buildClaimStaleAware`, or `claimVerdict` instead of at the `reclaimIfStale` call site. Why: `runIsHeld` is shared with non-claim-store, same-process callers that have no cross-machine clock problem to correct; editing it would be an out-of-scope, blast-radius-widening change for a fix that only needs to touch one function.

**Anti-pattern:** treating a `lease-lost` result from a failed CAS as retryable. Why: every current caller (`lights-out.js`, `cmdBuildClaim`) already surfaces the new holder and stops; a bare retry-and-force would reopen the exact double-drain this primitive exists to prevent. No caller does this today; this note exists so a future edit does not introduce it.

**Failure modes.** Every mode below is a tuning failure of a deliberately best-effort, bounded mitigation, not a claim that clock skew is fully solved. Skew larger than whatever tolerance actually applies (60s default and cross-box predicates only, 0s always for `recoveryClaimStore`) is unmitigated by this fix, exactly as it was on `main` before this ticket — those cases fall through to `confirmHead`'s CAS, which is what turns a wrong staleness verdict into a wasted reclaim attempt instead of a double-drain, whether or not the tolerance was involved at all.

- **The failure:** the 60-second default tolerance turns out too small for some operator's actual cross-box clock drift (an unmanaged host, no NTP). **How you'd know:** `reclaimIfStale` still reclaims a claim whose true holder is alive and heartbeating; the holder's subsequent `confirmHead` call fails with `superseded`, which is already logged distinctly in both `lights-out.js` and the `build-claim` CLI's refusal path. **What it means:** raise `FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS` for that environment; no code change is needed since the value is already externally configurable — this is the tolerance's escape hatch for exactly the "skew beyond the default is unmitigated" case named above.
- **The failure:** the tolerance is set too high (by an operator override), delaying reclaim of a genuinely crashed holder on an `applySkewTolerance: true` binding. **How you'd know:** the gap between a holder's last real heartbeat and a successful reclaim grows by roughly the tolerance value; visible in `faff build-claim reclaim` or `tidy`'s grooming output timestamps. **What it means:** lower the override; the 60-second default itself was chosen to keep this delay small relative to the 900-second heartbeat window (about 6.7 percent), so this is a risk of a bad override, not of the default. `recoveryClaimStore` is immune to this specific failure mode by construction (`applySkewTolerance: false` — no tolerance to mistune).

## 5. Design decision rationale

**Margin-based tolerance vs. a holder-side monotonic counter.** The ticket names both as acceptable fix directions, with the counter marked "preferred." A counter that the reader can trust without comparing wall clocks would need the holder to write an always-advancing generation number the reader observes directly, which means changing what `claim.json` carries and how the heartbeat writer (`heartbeat.js`) updates it. The ticket's own scope section says the fix "does not change the claim wire shape." **`**Chosen:**` the margin-based tolerance** satisfies the scope constraint, needs no new field, and is a two-line change at a single call site.

**Tolerance default: 60 seconds.** **`**Chosen:**` 60 seconds**, about 6.7 percent of the 900-second default heartbeat-stale window. Large enough to absorb realistic drift between two unsynchronized machines (NTP-synced hosts typically stay within a fraction of a second of each other; unmanaged clocks can drift by tens of seconds without correction), small enough that it barely delays reclaiming a genuinely crashed holder.

**Env var name: `FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS`, no config-file key.** **`**Chosen:**` mirrors `FAFF_RUN_HEARTBEAT_STALE_SECS`**, which is also an env-only override with no `.faffrc.yaml` counterpart. Consistent with the existing pattern rather than introducing a new one. This override is also the escape hatch named in Failure modes for the "skew beyond the tolerance is unmitigated" case — an operator is never stuck with the 60-second default.

**Per-predicate `applySkewTolerance` flag vs. a blanket call-site tolerance (round 2).** Round 1 of this spec applied `resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs` unconditionally at the `reclaimIfStale` call site, to every binding's `stalePredicate` alike. The round-1 adversarial spec review's architectural lens objected: applying the tolerance without regard to whether a given predicate's reclaim decision carries any destructive blast radius is a straight, unnecessary delay wherever it doesn't buy safety, and the recovery path in particular pays that delay for no offsetting benefit. **`**Chosen:**` a per-binding `applySkewTolerance` flag, consumed at the `reclaimIfStale` call site, defaulting to `true`.** The default stays `true` (not `false`) deliberately: an unmodified `buildClaimStore` and a not-yet-shipped `landingClaimStore` both need to keep the tolerance, and a default of `true` means neither has to declare anything to get it — only the one binding that should NOT pay the delay (`recoveryClaimStore`) opts out explicitly. A default of `false` would have been the more dangerous direction: any binding that forgot to opt in would silently regain zero tolerance, quietly reopening exactly the wrong-direction risk (a live cross-box holder misjudged stale) this ticket exists to close.

**`recoveryClaimStore` declares `applySkewTolerance: false` — zero added tolerance.** **`**Chosen:**` the recovery-claim reclaim path pays no delay beyond today's existing 900-second `heartbeatStaleSecs` window.** The reasoning does not depend on whether `recoveryClaimStore`'s underlying git-remote ref namespace can, in principle, be read from a different machine than wrote it — it can (the store's whole purpose, per its own header comment, is gating a "cross-box double-continue"). The reasoning instead turns on what a wrong verdict actually costs on this path versus the other two. On `buildClaimStore` and (once it ships) `landingClaimStore`, a reclaim that turns out to be wrong hands a build or a land to a second executor while the first is still actively, destructively working — the tolerance exists precisely to make that misjudgment rarer. On `recoveryClaimStore`, a reclaim that turns out to be wrong starts a *resume* of a stranded run segment a little early; per the WHY section's fail-safe principle, `confirmHead`'s CAS is unconditionally the actual backstop regardless of the tolerance, so the wrongly-reclaimed-from side's own `confirmHead` call refuses with `superseded` and it stops — the cost is one avoided-but-harmless resume attempt, not a double-drain, and the existing `hcReclaimB` fixture already exercises and accepts exactly this outcome as correct behaviour. Meanwhile a stranded segment sitting idle for an extra tolerance window before recovery even starts trying is a real, live cost with no corresponding safety upside on this path. Given that asymmetry — the tolerance buys real safety on the other two bindings and buys nothing on this one, while costing this one real recovery latency — zero tolerance is the better-tuned default for `recoveryClaimStore` specifically, independent of the same-box/cross-box framing either lens debates it in.

**Recovery-claim reclaim timing is unchanged by this spec, so `hcReclaimB` needs no edit.** Round 1 chose to bump the fixture's baked heartbeat age from 2000ms to 90000ms to keep `hcReclaimB.reclaimed === true` passing once a blanket tolerance reached this predicate. Round 2's `applySkewTolerance: false` choice above removes the need for that edit outright: `recoveryClaimStore` never receives the tolerance, so the fixture's original 2-second baked age keeps working exactly as it did on `main`. **`**Chosen:**` leave the fixture's numbers untouched and add the regression-guard test described in HOW instead of an edit-and-reverify pair.** This is a stronger form of the same assurance the round-1 objection asked for (a test that would fail if the fixture were coincidentally green): rather than proving a new number works and the old number would now fail — which no longer applies, because the old number never stops working — the guard proves the `applySkewTolerance: false` wiring itself is load-bearing, by showing the identical scenario WOULD flip to "held" (fail to reclaim) if `recoveryClaimStore` inherited the default tolerance instead of opting out.

**Problem 2: no logic change, coverage and documentation only.** **`**Chosen:**` after reading `reclaimIfStale`'s existing `--force-with-lease` fencing and the `pushX`/`pushY` selftest that already exercises it, the described TOCTOU window between two reclaimers is already closed.** The gap that remained was test coverage scoped to `recoveryClaimStore` only, and a comment that did not state the invariant explicitly enough to prevent this exact ticket. Both are additions, not corrections to broken logic. This conclusion is falsifiable by the new build-claims lease-race test; if it fails, the CAS is not what the code comments claim it is, and this rationale is wrong.

## 6. Open questions and assumptions

None. Every non-trivial decision above is marked `**Chosen:**`, and each is grounded in a specific line, function, or existing selftest rather than left open.

- [ ] `reclaimIfStale`'s staleness check no longer compares the reclaiming machine's raw `Date.now()` directly against a holder-written timestamp with zero tolerance, on bindings that need the tolerance.
- [ ] `confirmHead` remains the sole decider of who continues after a reclaim; no change weakens or bypasses it.
- [ ] The spec's WHY and Failure modes sections state plainly that the tolerance is a best-effort mitigation (skew beyond the configured value is unmitigated) and that it is operator-configurable — not framed as a complete fix.

- [ ] `resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs(env)` exists in `bundle.js`, defaults to 60, and is overridable via `FAFF_CLAIM_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_SECS` (finite, non-negative, else falls back to default).
- [ ] `claimStoreCore.reclaimIfStale` computes `toleranceSecs = spec.applySkewTolerance === false ? 0 : resolveClaimClockSkewToleranceSecs(env)`, then `skewedNowMs = Date.now() - toleranceSecs * 1000`, and passes `skewedNowMs` to `spec.stalePredicate` in place of a bare `Date.now()`.
- [ ] `recoveryClaimStore`'s spec object declares `applySkewTolerance: false`; `buildClaimStore`'s spec object declares no `applySkewTolerance` field (defaults to `true`).

- [ ] `runcheck.js` (`runIsHeld`, `heartbeatStaleSecs`) has no changes.
- [ ] `claim.json`'s shape and key order are unchanged for both bindings.
